cases.name: Susan "Phoenix" Lane-Fournier
cases.about:
She was described by friends as an outdoor enthusiast, dedicated to her work, and someone who was always willing to help others.

“We’re not going to let Phoenix’s light go out, and we’re going to let her light shine on anybody else that’s going through this and make sure they don’t have to go through this alone,” said Cari Gesch, friend of Phoenix, and one of the organizers of the community group that spread awareness of her disappearance online and through flyers until she was found. 

“We’re going to make sure her boys are taken care of because she’s not here,” Gesch added. “I’ve had a lot of titles in my life, but I’m most proud to be called a Mount Hood local.”

Some friends brought their dogs to the vigil to honor Elrond and Elros – Phoenix’s loyal dogs. At one point as people were sharing memories, the dogs in attendance began to howl and the people gathered joined in, lifting their voices to honor Phoenix.

Many spoke of Phoenix’s spirit, patience, quickness to befriend people and general kindness. A friend who worked similar shifts in a neighboring business to Hoodland Bazaar recalled the simple joy of seeing Phoenix “rolling up on her Harley in her skirt” to work.

Kate Brauner, who knew Phoenix for many years, spoke of meeting her when Brauner was a young yoga instructor.

“When I was in my early 20s, I was a yoga teacher and teaching classes and she came to one of my classes,” Brauner said. “She had some chronic pain. This was the first time in my young adult life that I was extraordinarily humbled and taught to hold space. I will never forget that exchange of spirit, of seeing someone struggling and just meeting them there. She was such a light, just so patient and gracious and giving. … She always held this amazing grace around my daughter who was rough and tumble. She just let her explore endlessly and indulge in her curiosities. She had such care for this community and was such a gift.”

The friend of Phoenix’s who adopted her two birds, Viki Adams McAbery, spoke of Phoenix’s effect on people.

“I’ve known Phoenix for a couple of years, and she was definitely the person that it took all of two seconds before her warmth ran right over you,” Adams McAbery said. “It gave you such a sense of joy and personal strength. … My saving grace is that I was gifted Phoenix’s birds. I thank Phoenix, because they embody the joy, (and) the same natural ability to spread their love. And the fact that I have them gives me solace to know that I do have a place in helping and being a part of Phoenix.”
cases.narrative: On 11/29/2024, her remains were discovered alongside a rural highway in northwest Oregon, near vacation cabins and hiking trails in the area of Mount Hood.
